anthropic/claude-opus-5-5.text:
verdict: needs-work
addresses-problem: yes — the in-scope widgets rows (download, column order, header-only empty export) are designed and tested; the 60s row is deferred to acme/widgets#78 per the user's answer C, and the mailer row is correctly marked elsewhere under the acme/mailer group.
findings:
- [major] gap @ "the mailer handoff reuses the existing export-ready event" — The spec does not say whether widgets emits this event, when it fires, or what payload it carries. The export is a synchronous GET that streams the file straight back, so no persisted artifact or download link exists for mailer's "export-ready email with the download link". → State whether widgets publishes the event (and at what point: request start, completion, or never) and which link it carries (e.g. the `/widgets/export.csv` URL). Otherwise state that no event emission is part of this change and mailer handles the trigger. Add a test for whichever emission is chosen. — probed: none
- [minor] oversimplification @ "Read widgets in id order in batches of 1000" — The spec does not cover a database error after headers and early batches are already sent. It also does not say whether all batches must come from one consistent snapshot, given rows can be inserted or deleted between batches. → Say whether the response is buffered or streamed. If streamed, define mid-stream failure behaviour (e.g. abort the connection so the file is visibly truncated). State whether batches use a single transaction or snapshot, or keyset paging on id. — probed: none
- [minor] ambiguity @ "The benchmark uses 10000 local widgets and measures from request start to the complete response" — The Design describes a benchmark for a row that is deferred to acme/widgets#78. Verification only says "when in-scope", which leaves an implementer unsure whether to build it now. → Mark the benchmark description as belonging to acme/widgets#78 and not delivered in this change, or drop it from the Design. — probed: none
- [minor] gap @ "Encode id, name, and status with standard CSV quoting" — Widget names are user-controlled. A name starting with `=`, `+`, `-` or `@` will be run as a formula when the CSV is opened in a spreadsheet, and the spec does not decide whether to neutralise this. → Decide whether to prefix such values (e.g. with `'`) or explicitly accept the risk, and cover the decision in the CSV escaping request test. — probed: none
lean: nothing to cut

anthropic/claude-opus-5-5.feedback: Neither output contains a finding of kind scope, so both facts hold in Before and After and nothing moved on this case. Before does carry an external-ref finding aimed at the 60s row's AC line (asking to restate the human's 'paging ships next sprint' reason) and a second ambiguity finding that leans on the #78 deferral while targeting the batching sentence, but both are typed external-ref/ambiguity, not scope, so a careful reader would not call them scope findings; After drops the external-ref one and reframes the batching finding as oversimplification about streaming/consistency, which is cleaner but was not required for the facts. Before's addresses-problem paragraph also explicitly invokes the old 'operates-without-it test' for the human-chosen deferral; After replaces that with 'deferred to acme/widgets#78 per the user's answer C', which is exactly the Change's intent (a quoted cut question plus human answer authorizes the cut) and should be kept. To be safe going forward, keep the After wording that cites the human answer as the provenance for the deferral and the acme/mailer group as settled attribution, and avoid re-introducing any finding that reads the deferral or the elsewhere disposition as a cut needing re-authorization.
